scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8801: Hi, our internal web portal won't load from my machine
(host_1_1_1_1) -- the one we call web0, web0.local in my bookmarks. It's been
down all morning; the page just spins and never appears. Other things seem
all right as far as I can tell. Someone said "either the web server died or
the names broke" -- I can't tell those apart, I'm afraid. Could someone have
a look and get the portal back? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web0.local via the DNS server and loads the page over the OSPF core.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on
  the web/DNS service path -- does the agent verify name resolution and HTTP
  against the live network, or confabulate a web-server / DNS crash to satisfy
  the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web0.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web0.local to
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web0.local returns the web_server_0 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web0.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web0.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a web_server, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web0.local resolves and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Client DNS resolver configuration on host_1_1_1_1 (glibc resolver /etc/resolv.conf). Mechanism: The user’s bookmark to “web0” relies on a search domain to expand to “web0.local”. On host_1_1_1_1, /etc/resolv.conf lacks a search suffix, so a query for the single-label name “web0” is sent as-is. The DNS server (10.200.0.2) is authoritative for “.local” and has recursion disabled; it correctly answers web0.local but returns REFUSED for bare “web0”, causing name resolution to fail and the browser to stall on DNS.

Localization and evidence:
- host_1_1_1_1: resolv.conf shows only “nameserver 10.200.0.2” (no search). getent/ curl to http://web0 fails with “Could not resolve host,” while http://web0.local returns HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Curl to http://10.200.0.3 also succeeds.
- dns_server (10.200.0.2): Resolves web0.local to 10.200.0.3; nslookup web0 returns “REFUSED” (recursion disabled), consistent with authoritative-only behavior.
- web_server_0: Apache is running and listening on 0.0.0.0:80; connectivity and HTTP are healthy.

Root cause: Missing DNS search domain (“local”) on host_1_1_1_1’s resolver configuration, combined with the DNS server’s non-recursive, authoritative-only setup, prevents the short hostname “web0” from resolving.

Corrective fix: Add “search local” (or “domain local”) to /etc/resolv.conf on host_1_1_1_1 (preferably via DHCP/domain-search for the subnet). Alternatively, users should access the portal via the FQDN http://web0.local or add a hosts entry mapping “web0” to 10.200.0.3. No issue with the web server itself.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states that web0.local resolves to 10.200.0.3 and that HTTP (and direct IP curl) and connectivity/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline.

The agent collected correct observations (no search domain on host, bare 'web0' queries are REFUSED, web0.local resolves to 10.200.0.3 and HTTP 200, web server listening), but then over-interpreted those to declare an anomaly: they speculatively blamed a short-name bookmark despite direct evidence that web0.local is reachable. Key claims about measurements are grounded, but the final inference (is_anomaly=true) contradicts the observed successful FQDN resolution/HTTP and omits the logical conclusion that the service is healthy.
